chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him)

about a man who married his slave woman to a free man, then said to her, 'When your husband dies, you will be free.' The husband died. He (the Imam) said: 'When the husband dies, she is free; she observes the waiting period of a free woman whose husband has died, and she has no inheritance from him because she became free after the husband's death.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever marries a slave woman while he has a free woman (wife), and she did not know about that, she is at choice until the end of the matter.
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance and waiting period ruling for a slave woman freed by her master after her free husband dies?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the specific juristic nuance that manumission occurring posthumously by the master's stipulation does not trigger inheritance rights, as the legal status change happens after the husband's death. The supplementary ruling by Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the principle of 'Ikhtiyar' (option), protecting the slave wife from being bound to a polygamous household she did not consent to, reflecting the Shia emphasis on consent in marital contracts.
